FULL EXPERIMENT PROTOCOL — BAdam vs LoRA on Llama 3-70B × MathInstruct, zero-shot math (DESIGN-ONLY; nothing was executed). 

=============================
0. VERDICT CRITERIA (pre-registered)
=============================
- Primary metric: unweighted macro-average zero-shot accuracy across the benchmark suite (each benchmark weighted equally regardless of size). Document: suite includes 6 benchmarks; core subset (GSM8K+MATH) also reported. 
- Primary claim: BAdam beats LoRA ⇔ Δ = macro(Default-LoRA→BAdam) > 0, judged on the DEFAULT LoRA arm. 
- Significance (required): per-benchmark paired McNemar exact test + paired bootstrap 95% CI on Δ; an effect is "supported" if Δ > 0 AND 95% CI excludes 0 (or lower bound comfortably > 0).
- Secondary (contextual, not verdict): memory/compute footprint per arm; matched-trainable-param LoRA arm; un-finetuned base floor.
- Decision rule fixed BEFORE training: no post-hoc benchmark dropping except pre-registered contamination exclusions.

=============================
1. BASE MODEL & HARDWARE (assumption, confirmed acceptable)
=============================
- Base: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B (non-chat) — chosen over instruct to isolate finetuning effect; flag: instruct variant is an unconfirmed alternative.
- Node: 1 × 8×H80-80GB (bf16), torch FSDP/ZERO-2 or DeepSpeed sharded training. 70B bf16 = 140GB → shard model across 8 GPUs (~17.5GB/GPU). BAdam: only active block's Adam states resident (D=20 → block ≈3.5B params → ~28GB states total, sharded). LoRA: adapter states tiny; base frozen 140GB sharded. Both feasible in bf16 → parity holds.

=============================
2. DATA PIPELINE (identical for ALL arms)
=============================
- Source: TIGER-Lab/MathInstruct (MAmmoTH, ICLR 2024) fields {instruction, output, dataset}, ~260K entries across 13 math subsets.
- Contamination control (pre-registered): drop any item whose normalized instruction string exactly matches a normalized eval test question from GSM8K-test, MATH-test, AQuA-test, TheoremQA, MiniF2F-valid, GSM-Hard. Cheap string-dedup before sampling.
- Subset pinning: SEED_DATA=20240601; shuffle surviving pool, take N=100,000; split: first 95,000 = train, next 5,000 = val (contiguous, seed-stable). Persist subset as parquet + recorded SHA-256 (reproducibility artifact).
- Template (identical both arms; base tokenizer has no chat control tokens, so use a stable instruction format):
  TRAIN: "<|begin_of_text|>Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.\n\n### Instruction:\n{instruction}\n\n### Response:\n{output}<|end_of_text|>"
  Tokenize with add_special_tokens=False; manual BOS/EOS.
- Loss masking: instruction segment → ignore_index=-100; only response tokens contribute to loss.
- Packing: pack tokenized samples into fixed contiguous blocks of max_seq_len=2048 separated by EOS; block assignment fixed via SEED_PACK (stored). The packed, tokenized, masked tensor artifact is built ONCE and reused by BOTH arms → byte-identical data order, batches, and loss masks across arms (strongest control).
- Val: 5,000 held-out items (same format) used ONLY for hyperparameter selection (LR grid), never for the verdict.

=============================
3. MATCHED TRAINING BUDGET (both arms)
=============================
- Optimizer steps: fixed token budget ≈ 2 epochs over the 95K train subset ≈ 150K optimizer steps equivalent... [corrected] ≈ ~95–100M effective train tokens; with global_batch = 64 sequences × 2048 tokens = 131,072 tokens/step → ~750 steps/epoch, ~1,500 total optimizer steps. Both arms run EXACTLY the same number of steps on the same packed artifact.
- Sequence len 2048; global batch 64 via micro-batch(2–4)×grad_accum(16–32); bf16; cosine LR schedule with 3% warmup; weight decay 0; β1=0.9, β2=0.999, eps=1e-8. Only peak LR may differ per method; LR tuned on val via small grid.
- Reproducibility: fixed RNG seeds for data, packing, and per-run op seeding; log and pin HF/transformers/pytorch versions and dataset revision.

=============================
4. ARM A — BADAM (full-param block-coordinate Adam)
=============================
- Block count D=20 → block = 4 consecutive of 80 layers; (sensitivity D ∈ {10,40} optional).
- Adam states ONLY for active block; block-phase update order = sequential 0→D-1 per cycle (default); one cycle = D block-phases.
- Block cycles = 2 (matches global 2-epoch token budget; total optimizer steps and token consumption identical to Arm B).
- Grid (on val): peak_lr ∈ {5e-5, 1e-4, 2e-4}; default 1e-4. Adam betas above; wd=0.
- Implementation: official BAdam repo block update logic (or faithful reimpl in PyTorch) with FSDP sharding; Adam states re-initialized per block-phase per the BAdam formulation.
- Record measured peak GPU memory (block states + activations).

=============================
5. ARM B1 — DEFAULT LoRA (primary comparator)
=============================
- PEFT LoRA: r=64, lora_alpha=128, dropout=0.1, bias=none, target_modules = attention only {q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj} → ≈335M trainable params (~0.5% of 70B) = "aggressive" practical LoRA.
- Grid (on val): peak_lr ∈ {1e-4, 2e-4, 5e-4}; default 2e-4. Same schedule/budget as Arm A.
- Primary conclusion judged against THIS arm.

=============================
6. ARM B2 — MATCHED-TRAINABLE-PARAM LoRA (exploratory/additive control)
=============================
- Rationale: BAdam's pitch is memory/param comparable to LoRA; a budget-matched LoRA disentangles "how many params trained" from "where placed". 
- r=32, lora_alpha=64, dropout=0.1, target_modules = ALL linear (q,k,v,o,up,gate,down) → ≈340M trainable params ≈ DEFAULT LoRA (335M) on an equal trainable-param budget with different rank/placement.
- Reported as additive exploratory column; NOT used for the primary verdict. 
- Rationale note: it tests concentration-vs-spread of the same param budget; also report peak optimizer-state memory for BAdam vs both LoRA variants as the direct "memory comparable to LoRA" claim check.

=============================
7. EVAL HARNESS (identical for all arms)
=============================
- Benchmarks (finalized): CORE = GSM8K-test (1,319) + MATH-test (5,000); EXTENSIONS = AQuA-test (254), TheoremQA (~800), MiniF2F-valid (~244), GSM-Hard (1,319). Total ≈ ~10.9K items.
- Prompt (fixed, base-friendly, matches training format):
  EVAL: "Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.\n\n### Instruction:\n{question}\n\n### Response:\nLet's think step by step."
- Decoding: PRIMARY = greedy (temperature=0, do_sample=False, top_p=1), max_new_tokens=1024 (GSM8K/MATH/GSM-Hard/MiniF2F) and 512 (AQuA/TheoremQA); stop at EOS. ROBUSTNESS (secondary) = temperature=0.2 sampling × 5 decode seeds → pass@1.
- Extract+Grade module (single shared function, per-dataset normalization):
  - GSM8K/GSM-Hard: final number after "####"/"The answer is"/last line → strip commas/$/spaces → exact digit match; fallback float compare.
  - MATH: last \boxed{...} or final expression → LaTeX-normalized string match (documented MATH grader).
  - AQuA: final option letter A–E → exact match.
  - TheoremQA: final number/expression → normalization + numeric tolerance where parseable.
  - MiniF2F: final number → normalization + exact/float match.
  - Unparseable generations = WRONG (never dropped; logged for audit) — no failure filtering.

=============================
8. ANALYSIS RECIPE (paired; shared item set across arms)
=============================
- Per item i, record correctness per arm → items are paired across arms on the same benchmark. 
- Per-benchmark accuracy; macro-average over the 6-benchmark suite (documented weighting; also report 2-benchmark core macro).
- Bootstrap 95% CI: resample items WITHIN each benchmark (maintaining arm-pairing), 10,000 reps → CI for each benchmark's Δ and for macro-Δ BAdam minus Default-LoRA.
- McNemar exact test per benchmark on discordant pairs (BAdam-right/LoRA-wrong vs LoRA-right/BAdam-wrong) → p-values (report exact binomial, no post-hoc corrections as exploratory but state them).
- Stability: repeat verdict across the 5 decode seeds → report mean±range of macro-Δ; primary macro uses greedy.
- Report tables: columns = {Base floor, BAdam, Default LoRA, Matched LoRA} × rows = {each benchmark acc, macro}, plus memory/step-time secondary; the verdict line = BAdam − Default LoRA Δ with CI + McNemar.

=============================
9. CONTROLS (sanity/confounds)
=============================
- Same packed data artifact, same batch stream, same schedule, same decoding/prompts/graders across arms (only update method differs).
- Un-finetuned base evals = floor control to confirm finetuning changes scores directionally.
- Contamination dedup vs eval tests (pre-registered).
- Optional LoRA variant isolates param-budget-vs-placement.
- Per-method LR tuned on val only; verdict fixed before running.

=============================
10. FEASIBILITY (as approved: 8×H80 bf16 parity) + FALLBACK
=============================
- Training FLOPs ≈ 6×70e9×~100e6 ≈ 4.2e19/epoch-ish → at 8×H100 (~7.9e15 FLOP/s bf16) ≈ 1.5 h/epoch @100% MFU, ~4 h @40%; ×2 arms ×2 epochs ≈ ~16–32 h node-time + LR tuning; evals: ~10.9K genres × ~400 tok ≈ ~4.4M eval tokens/arm ≈ negligible. Total ≈ 2–4 days inclusive (tuning, evals, failures) — order-of-magnitude, hardware assumed.
- LOWER-HARDWARE FALLBACK (explicit, NOT the verdict path): any quantization (QLoRA 4/8-bit) or CPU-offload asymmetry breaks bf16 parity → do NOT report those runs as the verdict. If compute is insufficient for the full protocol: run a small PILOT (e.g., 5–10K subset, 1 block-cycle, ~200–300 steps) purely to (a) validate harness/reproducibility, (b) LR sanity (loss decreases, no NaN, eval pipeline & grader run end-to-end). The verdict is NEVER taken from the pilot — it must come from the full-budget data on the verified harness.

=============================
11. EXPLICIT NO-CLAIM STATEMENT
=============================
This is a design-only deliverable. Nothing was installed, trained, or evaluated in this sandbox (no GPU, no network, no packages, /workspace contains only task.json with the 'design-only' note). All numbers above are targets/estimates to be realized by the future run, not results.
